abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Solid-state batteries are a transformational and intrinsically safe energy storage solution. However, progress has been limited by high solid-solid interfacial impedance and numerous reports of Li-dendrites. By modifying the electrolyte composition and interface in a rationally designed 3D architecture we have been able to overcome these limitations achieving both high energy density and cycling rates of 100 mA/cm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    at room temperature with no applied pressure. The science and engineering of this technology will be described as well as the path to commercialization and lessons learned in that endeavor.
                  </jats:p>
